payload.summary: Completed both authorized screens with 13 successful native runs and 13 audits, all with leakage_flag=false. Return to independent A review.
payload.scientific_result: Support revision produced small gains that weakened under mismatch. Explicit operator uncertainty improved additive-shift recovery while sacrificing some clean validation performance. The selected support-revising model achieved validation/audit recovery of 0.9066/0.9130; the selected uncertainty model achieved 0.9024/0.9195. Reproduced OMP validation recovery was 0.904858. Across three additive-0.30 operator realizations, uncertainty-aware recovery averaged 0.787052 versus OMP's 0.771557, improving in every realization. Under gain-0.30 changes, it averaged 0.784904 versus 0.775576, but lost in one realization. These are conditional improvements, not established hidden-test gains.
limitations: Hidden-test recovery, reward and the hidden operator relationship remain unknown.

The uncertainty method combines covariance modeling, coefficient shrinkage and support weighting; its gains do not isolate covariance modeling from ordinary regularization.
The uncertainty model does not estimate or calibrate the test operator.

Reconstructed normalized OMP k=6 exactly reproduced reported validation recovery, 0.904858. It remained the common reference across both screens.

Seven settings covered subspace pursuit, hard-threshold pursuit and convex sparse initialization with debiasing. Training-only selection chose subspace pursuit k=6. Its validation advantage over OMP was 0.001696 clean, but averaged -0.001132 under additive-0.30 mismatch. Support revision alone did not consistently recover the remaining error.

Six settings explicitly represented signal-dependent additive or gain uncertainty in residual covariance. Training-only selection chose additive uncertainty tau=0.10 with k=6. Under additive-0.30 mismatch, false-positive relative energy fell from 0.110687 for matched ordinary subspace pursuit to 0.096004. Stronger uncertainty settings impaired clean recovery.

mechanism_observations.observation: The reconstructed fixed-k=6 normalized OMP control exactly reproduced historical validation recovery, 0.904858. payload.summary: Completed the authorized shared screen. Recommend SP-support ridge for independent A review under the declared development criterion.
payload.scientific_result: Constant ridge on fixed SP6 supports scored 0.822129 on training-only development, versus 0.817729 for the retained uncertainty package. Across five additional training resamples, its advantage was 0.003768, with conditional row-cluster 95% interval [0.002510, 0.004983], exceeding the prespecified 0.002 margin. Stabilization improved shifted recovery primarily by reducing false-positive energy, while sacrificing clean recovery. Energy association and measurement-noise geometry supplied no consistent incremental benefit. Support-revision effects varied by operator. Three new native runs and submissions succeeded with leakage_flag=false.

mechanism_findings.finding: The shared screen evaluated the exact restored independent-regression model on common validation observations. Recovery was 0.128027 clean, 0.107112 averaged across three additive shifts, and 0.108985 across three gain shifts. It substantially trails sparse inversion. Historical model availability is resolved; original training-source reproduction remains unavailable.

The exact restored joint-regression model scored 0.133245 clean, 0.112784 under additive shifts and 0.114443 under gain shifts on the same validation cases. Shared inverse regularization slightly improves on independent regression but does not approach sparse forward recovery. Original historical training-source reproduction remains unavailable.

Exact retained fixed OMP scored 0.904858/0.771557/0.775576 across clean/additive/gain conditions. Exact retained adaptive OMP scored 0.904214/0.671390/0.684960. Thus the historical adaptive rule retains clean performance but deteriorates substantially under these repeated operator shifts. Fixed-OMP reconstruction matched retained predictions within 8.19e-14.

With the same ridge penalty and estimated operator, initial SP support revision improved clean resample recovery over OMP by 0.002566 and reduced omitted true energy by 0.001476. Additive/gain recovery improvements were smaller, 0.000854/0.000246, with operator-dependent reversals. L1 remains a strong clean rival at 0.914229 validation recovery. Support correction helps conditionally but does not explain all stabilization gains.

Matched comparisons now cover the selected k=6, tau=0.1 configuration. Across resamples, associated energy penalties versus distribution-matched permuted penalties changed aggregate recovery by -0.000116, with conditional interval [-0.000620, 0.000395]. Heterogeneous noise weighting versus isotropic treatment changed recovery by -0.000084. Uncertainty-stage support reconsideration produced mixed effects. These probes supply no consistent uncertainty-specific incremental benefit and do not identify a physical uncertainty cause.

Fixed-SP-support ridge improved additive/gain resample recovery over least-squares by 0.015590/0.018584 while holding omitted energy unchanged. Reduced false-positive energy supplied most of the improvement; clean recovery decreased by 0.004195. Three coefficient-rule models completed native runs and submissions with finite audits and leakage_flag=false.
